title: From O(n) Iterations to O(1): The Digital Root Formula
body: The naive approach iterates digit summation until reaching a single digit, which requires O(log n) iterations each taking O(log n) time. The closed-form formula dr(n) = 1 + ((n-1) mod 9) computes the result in constant time using a single modular reduction.

title: Idempotency: The Fixed-Point Property
body: digitalRoot_idempotent shows dr(dr(n)) = dr(n): once you've computed the digital root, applying it again gives the same result. The proof uses the fact that dr(n) is always a single digit (1-9), so digitalRoot_single gives dr applied to a single digit is the identity.
